scope: Chs. 8-10 (pp.131-225) + Introduction (Principal Claims/Synopsis) + Conclusions (pp.226-228). Ch.10 'Feeling Fantastic Again' (pp.182-225) is the cluster keystone. Parts 1-2 (rhetoric-as-proof; the supposed contradiction) read for framing only.
abstract_paraphrase: Dow argues that for Aristotle in the Rhetoric, arousing an audience's passions can amount to giving them proper grounds for conviction (pistis), so emotion-arousal is a genuine technical proof. This requires that the passions be representational states in which the subject TAKES THINGS TO BE as represented. Aristotle's theory (Rhet. 2.1-11) is that passions ARE pleasures and pains (Claim 1) that are intentional/representational, felt AT a target and ON grounds (Claim 2). The representational capacity is phantasia; but the ATTITUDE the subject takes toward phantasia's evaluative content, in a passion, is AFFIRMATION by the subject herself (not merely a part of her soul). Against the 'mere/uncommitted appearance' reading (Cooper, Sihvola, Striker; qualifiedly Moss), Dow argues affirmation is what makes recalcitrant passions genuinely conflicted/inconsistent (a desideratum a good theory must meet), and that the DA 3.3 sun-illusion is DISANALOGOUS to passion (no inconsistency there) - so the visual-illusion model fails for emotion. Affirmation is a relational, person-level, gradable treating-as-true, distinct from full doxa/pistis.

outline.summary: Principal claim: arousing passions can give proper grounds for conviction, so it is part of rhetoric. Two foundations: (1) normative rhetoric-as-pistis (Part 1); (2) passions as representational states in which the subject takes things to be as represented (Part 3). If passions involved NO affirmation of content, their arousal could not be a technical proof. Dow rejects the 'merely appear' reading; passions involve phantasia whose contents are (at least to some degree) taken to be the way things actually are.

Rhet. 2.1 1378a19-22 as a DEFINITION of the passions: states on account of which we change/differ in relation to our judgements (kriseis), accompanied by pain and pleasure. krisis chosen because rhetoric operates in courts/assemblies (verdicts), NOT (pace Sihvola) to stay neutral between belief/appearance or to allow animal pathe. 1377b31-1378a5: Aristotle switches indifferently between 'appears' (phainetai) and 'believes' (dokei). Integrated reading: passions are representational states constituting the subject's overall outlook, with pleasure/pain at the represented circumstances; handles enmity (no pain), hunger, headache counterexamples (8.6).

Rhet. 2.1-11 is Aristotle's OWN, still-credible theory (pace Cooper 'dialectical'; Striker 'imported'; Frede 'Philebus mixed pleasure-pain'). Claim 1: a passion IS pleasure/pain (philology of hepetai 'accompanies'; 6 passions defined as pains, 3 as pleasures, up to 11/17). Claim 2: that pleasure/pain is intentional - AT a target, ON grounds (1378a22-4 schema; epi+dat etc.). Representational pleasure: against 'restoration of nature' reading of Rhet. 1.11 (1369b33-1370a18); via Philebus 31b-36c and Timaeus 64c-e, pleasure/pain are perceptual, representational, falsifiable. Merit: pleasure/pain is NOT the genus of emotion (9.6).

KEYSTONE. Four questions distinguished (faculty / attitude / fit-with-phantasia-psychology / passion-belief conflict). Dow has CHANGED HIS MIND (vs Dow 2009): a passion constitutes affirmation by the subject HERSELF of phantasia's content. 10.2 five recalcitrance desiderata + 'adult humans don't wholly repudiate their passions' (DA 3.3 427b21-4). 10.3 two arguments that passions involve phantasia (parts of soul; pleasure/pain). 10.4 AFFIRMATION specified: relational, person-level, not a separate act; person-vs-faculty (Insomn. crossed fingers 461b2-5); evidence from Rhet. 2.2-11 phantasia-terminology + DA 3.3 427b16-24 (belief causes passion, uncommitted phantasia does not). 10.4.4 the sun (DA 3.3 428a18-b9) vs the mixture view (Sophist 263d-264b): sun-illusion involves NO inconsistency, so DISANALOGOUS to recalcitrant passion which IS conflicted/irrational - the visual-illusion model fails for emotion. 'some level of affirmation.'

Regulation: (a) whether a phantasma is affirmed depends on a more authoritative faculty being active (DA 3.3 429a5-8); (b) evaluative phantasmata of pleasant/painful have NECESSARY motivational consequences regardless of belief (De Motu 8 701b33-702a2). 'Covering-over' of reason is a matter of DEGREE (Insomn. 460b11-16); passions can themselves cover over reason (citing Moss 2009). Why only EVALUATIVE phantasia must 'listen to reason' (EN 1.13 1102b13-33). Painting case (DA 3.3 427b23-4) reread via Rep. 10 596d-e as phantasia successfully concurring with reason. 10.6 recalcitrance = TWO malfunctions; the conflicts Aristotle actually recognizes (Odysseus EN 7.6 1149a21-b26; appetite-akrasia DA 3.10 433b5-10) are NOT direct contradictions of the passion's representation.

Merits: meets all 5 desiderata; avoids OVERSTATING the failing (recalcitrant emotion less bad than inconsistent beliefs, since reason is the 'ruling' part); sometimes passion tracks evidence better than belief (EN 7.6 1151b17-22). 10.8: passions = phantasia-exercises with affirmed evaluative content; explains legitimate rhetorical use + why virtue (unconflicted affirmation) beats self-control. Conclusions: FICTION left UNRESOLVED - dilemma between malfunction and taking-fiction-as-real; gestures via Poetics 1451a36-b10 that tragic pity/fear may target universal human truths. Animals: human/non-human passions differ 'by the more and the less' (HA 8.1 588a18-30).

concepts.label: passion-arousal as proper grounds for conviction (pistis)
concepts.gloss: the book's master claim: arousing audience passions can constitute giving them justified grounds for accepting a premise, hence emotion-arousal is a genuine technical proof (entechnos pistis).

concepts.label: affirmation by the subject herself
concepts.gloss: Dow's central thesis (changed from Dow 2009): in having a passion the subject AS A WHOLE (not only a sub-personal part) affirms that things are as phantasia represents them; the attitude that makes passions usable as premises.

concepts.label: affirmation as relational, non-act, gradable (NOT a separate assent)
concepts.gloss: to 'affirm' phantasia's content is to be disposed to treat it as giving the way things are UNLESS a more authoritative faculty overrides; not an extra act of assent over and above phantasia/nous; admits of 'levels' / degrees. Hence distinct from Stoic synkatathesis and from all-or-nothing pistis.

concepts.label: person-level vs faculty-level affirmation
concepts.gloss: Insomn. 461b2-5 (crossed fingers): content can be affirmed by the capacity that presents it OR by the person as a whole; Dow's claim concerns the latter - where his account goes beyond Moss's sub-personal 'acceptance' (10.4.1 n.48).

concepts.label: passions as pleasures and pains (Claim 1)
concepts.gloss: to have a passion IS to experience pain, pleasure, or both; defended by the philology of hepetai ('accompanies/follows') and the Rhet. 2.2-11 definitions (6 pains, 3 pleasures, up to 11/17).

concepts.label: representational/intentional pleasure-and-pain (Claim 2)
concepts.gloss: the pain/pleasure is AT the passion's 'target' and ON its 'grounds' (1378a22-4), representing the target in ways that give grounds for that emotion; pleasure/pain themselves are falsifiable representational events (Timaeus 64c-e).

concepts.label: target vs grounds of a passion
concepts.gloss: Aristotle's three-part schema (how disposed / at whom / on what grounds); Dow shows targets and grounds rarely come apart - a passion just is representing facts about its object (epi+dat etc.).

concepts.label: the 'merely/uncommitted appearance' (non-judgmental) reading - rejected
concepts.gloss: the view (Cooper, Sihvola, Striker; qualifiedly Moss) that passionate phantasia can be 'non-epistemic'/wholly unendorsed; Dow rejects it because an uncommitted appearance cannot ground conviction and cannot capture recalcitrant conflict.

concepts.label: passions exercise phantasia not doxa/reason
concepts.gloss: two arguments: the passions belong to the non-reasoning part (DA 1.1 403a; EN 1.13; Rhet. 1.10 alogos orexis), and they involve sensory pleasure/pain which involves phantasia (Rhet. 1.11 1370a27-32; Phys. 7.3 247a7-18).

concepts.label: recalcitrant emotions + five desiderata
concepts.gloss: cases where emotion persists in recognized conflict with better belief; a theory must (1) not make them impossible, (2) explain usual belief-tracking, (3) account for the conflict, (4) account for the failing, (5) not overstate the failing. Dow's affirmation-account meets all five.

concepts.label: the sun-illusion DISANALOGY (the keystone argument)
concepts.gloss: DA 3.3 428a18-b9: the foot-wide sun involves NO subject-level inconsistency (belief 'sun is huge' is wholeheartedly endorsed), so a belief/affirmation theory is BAD for it - but recalcitrant passion IS conflicted/irrational, so the visual-illusion model fails for emotion and the passions DO involve affirmation.

concepts.label: the Platonic 'mixture view' of appearance (Sophist) - Aristotle's target
concepts.gloss: phantasia = doxa + aisthesis, with belief explaining appearance-falsity (Sophist 263d-264b); the sun case is Aristotle's objection to it; Dow surveys Hamlyn/Lycos, Hicks/Everson, and his preferred 'in his view' reading of b7-8.

concepts.label: evaluative phantasmata have necessary motivational consequences
concepts.gloss: De Motu 8 701b33-702a2: phantasia of the pleasant/painful is 'necessarily' accompanied by heating/chilling, hence motivation, EVEN against more authoritative belief; explains why only evaluative phantasia must 'listen to reason.'

concepts.label: 'covering-over'/disabling of reason by degree
concepts.gloss: Insomn. 460b11-16: reason's impairment by fever (and by passion: DA 3.3 429a7) is graded ('if not excessively ill...if more severe'); when reason is disabled, normally-unaffirmed phantasmata become affirmed and acted on; Dow cites Moss 2009 for the passion-disables-reason mechanism.

concepts.label: evaluative phantasia 'listening to reason' / concurring
concepts.gloss: EN 1.13 1102b13-33: the non-reasoning part should heed reason 'as a father'; in the virtuous it 'completely concurs'; Aristotle imposes this ONLY on evaluative (motivational) phantasia, not on memory/dreams/the sun.

concepts.label: two malfunctions in recalcitrant passion
concepts.gloss: (1) the passion's evaluative representation is not regulated by reason; (2) the less-authoritative phantasma stays affirmed and motivationally live when the subject should be uncommitted to it - a genuine but not-too-severe failing.

concepts.label: virtue better than self-control via unconflicted affirmation
concepts.gloss: 10.8: the virtuous make an UNCONFLICTED affirmation of the correct appraisal; the self-controlled also carry a 'dissenting voice' (an incorrect passionate appraisal) - which is the failing.

concepts.label: passion at fiction as unresolved dilemma
concepts.gloss: Conclusions (pp.226-8): pity/fear at known fiction forces EITHER psychological malfunction OR taking the fictional objects to be real; Dow gestures (Poetics 1451a36-b10) that we may really respond to UNIVERSAL human truths, but does not resolve. [T1-4 hook]

concepts.label: the painting case as successful concurrence
concepts.gloss: DA 3.3 427b23-4 (unmoved 'as by a painting'): reread via Rep. 10 596d-e as a case where recognizing image-as-image shifts the content ('what fearful things look like'), so phantasia concurs with reason and is NOT affirmed.

concepts.label: common-phantasia continuity of human/animal passions
concepts.gloss: HA 8.1 588a18-30: human and non-human passions deploy the SAME kinds of process, differing only 'by the more and the less' (complexity of affirmed content), not analogically; a softer line than Konstan's animal-denial.

readings.thesis: For Aristotle, arousing the passions can give an audience proper grounds for conviction; hence emotion-arousal is a genuine part of rhetorical expertise.
Aristotle's passions are pleasures and pains (Claim 1) that are intentional and representational (Claim 2): pain/pleasure AT a target, ON grounds.
The representational capacity exercised in the passions is phantasia, not doxa/reason (passions belong to the non-reasoning part; they involve sensory pleasure/pain which involves phantasia).

KEYSTONE (judgmental pole): in having a passion the subject HERSELF affirms phantasia's evaluative content as the way things are - so passions can be acceptances of premises; against the 'uncommitted appearance' reading.

'Affirmation' is a relational, person-level, GRADABLE treating-as-true (no extra act of assent), distinct from full doxa/pistis/conviction - so it can stand against a contrary belief (recalcitrance) without flat self-contradiction in one faculty.
readings.axis: nature of the attitude: affirmation != doxa (decides the diss's doxa-mapping)

readings.thesis: The DA 3.3 sun-illusion is DISANALOGOUS to recalcitrant passion: the sun-case involves NO subject-level inconsistency (the belief 'sun is huge' is uncompromised), so a belief/affirmation theory is bad for it but good for the passions, which ARE conflicted/irrational. The visual-illusion model thus fails for the emotions.
readings.axis: cognitive-evaluative<->quasi-perceptual: inverts Moss's use of the sun passage

readings.thesis: Recalcitrant passions are genuine MALFUNCTIONS (two failings), and Aristotle has the resources to explain them; the conflicts he actually foregrounds are not direct contradictions of the passion's representation but disputes over the all-things-considered verdict.

Evaluative phantasmata of the pleasant/painful have NECESSARY motivational consequences regardless of conflicting belief; this (not Moss's 'default yielding') explains the persisting pull and why only evaluative phantasia must 'listen to reason.'
Aristotle's account leaves passion at known FICTION unresolved (malfunction vs taking-fiction-as-real); a Poetics-based escape is that we respond to universal human truths.
Human and non-human passions deploy the SAME kinds of process (common phantasia), differing only 'by the more and the less' (complexity of affirmed content) - a graded continuity, not mere analogy.

aristotle_loci.role: THE definition of the passions: states on account of which we change/differ pros tas kriseis (judgements), accompanied by pain and pleasure [ch.8 core; ch.9; ch.10.3.2]
rhetoric is for the sake of a krisis (assembly/jury verdict); get oneself and the listener in the right condition - frames the krisis reading

things 'appear' (phainetai) different to friendly/hostile, hopeful/pessimistic; the listener 'believes' (dokei) - Aristotle switches indifferently between appears/believes [the dissertation's pathetic-loop sibling passage, read by Dow as outlook-influence]
three-part schema for each passion (how disposed / at whom / on what grounds = target vs grounds)
definition of anger: desire-cum-pain for APPARENT (phainomene) revenge on account of an APPARENT slight - the phantasia-terminology Dow reads as 'how the subject takes things to be'
the pleasures of anger signalled as exercises of phantasia (Dow: compatible with denying phantasia gives the OBJECT's representation)
calmness: anger abates toward those who 'appear' innocent/involuntary - Dow's strongest case that 'apparent' = affirmed-to-be (an unendorsed thought won't quell anger)
definition of fear: pain/disturbance from the APPEARANCE of future destructive/painful harm
definition of pity: pain at APPARENT undeserved destructive harm, foreseeable for oneself, appearing near - Dow's running example of affirmed content
anger (orge) and appetite (epithymia) as non-reasoning desire (alogos orexis) - argument that passions are not reasoning-based
definition of pleasure ('motion of the soul...'); Dow argues AGAINST the 'restoration of nature' reading, FOR a representational pleasure
pleasure is in perceiving a condition; phantasia is 'weak perception'; remembering/anticipating bring phantasia + pleasure - pleasure involves phantasia
the simultaneous/subsequent/potential distinction for 'goes with' (hepetai) - philology of the passion-pleasure connection

phantasia != hypolepsis: believing something fearsome immediately causes a passion, whereas with phantasia we are 'as if looking at a painting' - Dow's 2nd argument FOR affirmation (belief causes passion, uncommitted phantasia does not)
the foot-wide SUN passage: argument that phantasia is not doxa/mixture; Dow's DISANALOGY keystone (no inconsistency in the sun case, unlike recalcitrant passion)
animals/some humans 'act according to phantasia' because they lack nous or nous is 'covered over' by passion/disease/sleep - the locus for relational, override-governed affirmation
imagined terrible things leave us unmoved 'as by a painting' - reread (via Rep. 10) as evaluative phantasia successfully concurring with reason; ALSO the 'wholly repudiated fear -> no fear' datum
passions are body-involving enmattered logoi; anger = boiling of blood around the heart; the small-stimulus/no-stimulus fear cases as body-condition divergences from belief

appetite-akrasia: appetite's verdict 'unqualifiedly pleasant and good' (b9) conflicts with reason re the future/now; nous and epithymia each 'assert' - a conflict NOT over the object's representation directly
the bearer of desire/aversion is 'not a different thing' from the perceptual bearer though its being is different - supports locating passions with the perceptive/phantastic part
Aristotle's caution about 'parts' of the soul; distinguishing psychological capacities
fever makes animals appear on the walls; if not too ill, the falsity does NOT escape notice; if more severe, 'they even move toward them' - reason's disabling by DEGREE; passions can do likewise
the cognitions of the controlling part and the appearance-producing part 'do not involve the same faculty' - distinct-capacities ground for passion/belief conflict
crossed-fingers: 'the origin AFFIRMS what comes from each sense unless a more authoritative one contradicts' - the PERSON-vs-FACULTY affirmation text; 'we do not affirm two' (460b21)
finger-under-eyeball: one object seen as two; uncommitted phantasia, subject explicitly rejects it as false
evaluative phantasmata of pleasant/painful 'necessarily' accompanied by heating/chilling (motivation), regardless of belief - the mechanism of persisting motivational pull
the non-reasoning part that 'has reason' by heeding it; submits in the self-controlled, 'completely concurs' (b28) in the virtuous - location and regulation of the passions
thumos-akrasia: Odysseus's anger (Od.20); reason agrees a slight occurred and grants some vengeance-impulse, disputes only 'one should fight' (a33-4) - conflict NOT over the representation
body-altering pathos; 'has and doesn't have' knowledge - Dow cites Moss 2009's reading that the passions themselves disable reason
the passion may sometimes track the evidence better than reasoned belief (its persistence then a merit); akrasia renders the subject 'conflicted'
by passions I mean the things accompanied by pleasure/pain (appetite, anger, fear...); virtue as the right condition re passions
the passions should be felt at the right things etc. as correct reason prescribes; role of upbringing (cf. Burnyeat 1980)
anger and fear do not 'settle down' (kathistatai) despite efforts - Dow reads as bodily persistence rather than persisting misrepresentation
the 'perceptive and desiderative' part as one faculty; passions accompanied by SENSORY (aisthetike) pleasure/pain
acquiring virtue involves alteration of the AISTHETIC part; the hexeis of the soul don't change but the pathe do; pleasures/pains as alterations of the sensitive part
the principle of non-contradiction at the level of belief - background to why knowingly holding p and not-p is irrational (10.4.4)
human and non-human passions differ 'by the more and the less' - the graded-continuity reading of animal pathe
tragic pity/fear; the connection of staged action to UNIVERSAL truths - the (unresolved) fiction escape-route
endorsed emotional responses to music/tragedy; 'the passionate part' (to pathetikon meros)

aes_internal: aes-03/aes-04 Moss (2009; 2012a) - cited PERVASIVELY in ch.10 (the principal interlocutor): allied on phantasia involvement, on DA 3.10/EN 7.3 complementarity ('justly celebrated Moss 2009'), and on passions disabling reason; OPPOSED on whether the attitude is non-doxastic acceptance (Moss) or subject-level affirmation (Dow); Dow's n.48 marks his person-level move beyond Moss's sub-personal 'acceptance'

aes-01 Fortenbaugh (1971; 2002) - belief-view ALLY but corrected: Dow agrees the subject takes-things-to-be-so but locates the capacity in phantasia not doxa, and rejects Fortenbaugh's causes-not-passions thesis (Dow 2011, 58-9)
aes-02 Konstan (2006, ch.1, ch.3) - cited for pathe ~ emotions and for praotes as a positive emotion; Dow's common-phantasia continuity is softer than Konstan's animal-denial
opposes: the 'mere/uncommitted appearance' non-judgmental reading shared by Cooper, Sihvola, Striker, and (qualifiedly) Moss

tensions.desc: Dow is the ALLY: passions involve the subject's affirming their content (else they couldn't be pisteis), directly opposing Moss's non-doxastic reading and underwriting that aroused civic emotions = reasonable acceptance of premises.

Dow's 'affirmation' is NOT full doxa/pistis: it is a non-reasoning-part, relational, gradable, non-act treating-as-true (distinct faculty from doxa; not Stoic synkatathesis). The dissertation must decide whether its 'doxa = taking-as-true' maps onto Dovian affirmation (then recast as non-doxastic) or onto reasoning-part doxa proper (then argue civic emotions engage reason specifically).

Same sun passage (DA 3.3 428a-b9), opposite use: Moss = paradigm of non-doxastic default-yielding motivation; Dow = DISANALOGY (no inconsistency in the sun case) proving passions, unlike the sun-illusion, involve subject-level affirmation. The cluster's sharpest disagreement.

Dow concedes evaluative phantasmata exert NECESSARY motivational pressure even against belief (De Motu 8), which is close to Moss's persisting-pull datum; he must distinguish this (a malfunction + body-grounded pressure) from Moss's 'default yielding by reason's failure-to-oppose.'

Dow leaves passion at known FICTION explicitly UNRESOLVED (malfunction vs taking-as-real), offering only a Poetics 'universal truths' gesture. The dissertation can borrow the gesture but must supply the resolution Dow withholds; bears on grief / emotions toward non-realizable goods.

Dow admits an unexplained asymmetry: why humans more reliably withhold affirmation from NON-evaluative than from evaluative phantasmata when each conflicts with better belief, given phobics' reason seems unimpaired (10.6-10.7). The affirmation-account's open edge.

dissertation_hooks.T1-2: PRIMARY ALLY source; defends the affirmation/taking-as-true reading against recalcitrance; supports the two-tier reconciliation by supplying the ATTITUDE (affirmation) at both tiers while Moss supplies the lower-tier mechanism
dissertation_hooks.T1-2-doxa-mapping: affirmation != doxa: relational, person-level, gradable, non-act, non-reasoning-part - decides whether the diss's 'taking-as-true' should be recast as Dovian affirmation or defended as reasoning-part doxa for civic emotions
dissertation_hooks.T1-2-recalcitrance: the sun-illusion DISANALOGY is the keystone reply: concede sun/wall-cracks to Moss as non-doxastic illusion; insist emotions proper carry subject-level affirmation (hence genuine conflict), which is what makes their arousal a legitimate pistis
dissertation_hooks.T1-4-fiction-grief: fiction left UNRESOLVED (malfunction vs taking-as-real); Poetics 'universal truths' gesture available for emotions toward non-actual/non-realizable objects
dissertation_hooks.animal-pathos: common-phantasia, 'more-and-less' continuity (HA 8.1 588a18-30): animals have simpler affirmations of simpler content, not merely analogical pathe - a graded alternative to a hard rational-only line
